title: Game Bridges or Game remixing (Minecraft x GTA, Halo x Animal Crossing...)
author: LudwigLoewenlunte
selftext:
Hey everyone,

We're all seeing the rise of AI everywhere. Even here on Reddit, even in gaming subs. If this is too AI-heavy, feel free to remove it, but I just find this stuff way too fascinating not to share.

I've spent the last two hours going down a YouTube rabbit hole watching **game-mixing videos**, where entire game mechanics and systems from different games are combined.

It started with **Minecraft in GTA**. And you can actually interact with the world! Shoot ~~pedestrians~~ bad guys with a bow, place dynamite next to cars and watch them explode.

Then there's **Tony Hawk in Call of Duty**.

And then there's [Super Mario 64 in Elden Ring](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jp7hM1vKRpY&t=154s). At first you're like, "Okay, that's pretty cool." Until Mario grabs Margit by the tail and starts swinging him around like Bowser in the N64 days. HOLY SHIT.

Some of these [YouTube videos are already 9 days old](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z6GbWl3BLpM), and I barely see anyone talking about this.

All of this is becoming possible because people are starting to [decompile and reverse-engineer games](https://medium.com/@azzogs.asteroid/game-bridges-are-here-reverse-engineering-enables-game-mixing-7c088611abca).

Sure, you could argue that these are all just unplayable prototypes right now. But give it another six months...

**What do you guys think about this?** What about the ethical and legal implications? Or is there a game mashup you've always dreamed of playing?

comments.author: Material-Database-24
comments.body:
If you own the game binaries, you are kinda free to do so. Privately, for your own use.

But good luck if you ever make the mistake and publish those..

In bigger picture.. well, this is not really anything new, except it is now super easy and fast. I expect we in future see game assets being encrypted and requiring internet and call home to be decrypted at runtime. Yay!

I must say, it's a bit perplexing when C++ games are recompiled into Rust that 1) isn't OO with inheritance (well, it can bend to similar structure) and 2) doesn't allow "half" (I mean, some probably do, but Rust's memory safety is super strict vs C++..) the optimization methods used in C++ games.. does the AI "fill the blanks" from it's own? Kinda sorta makes it a different game then, even if it runs the same. It's usually easier to port from stricter to more lose.
